title: Class 11 Chemistry — Bio-inorganic Chemistry Study Guide
notes: Bio-inorganic chemistry studies inorganic elements and metal ions in living systems. Macronutrients are required in relatively large amounts; micronutrients in trace amounts. This classification describes required quantity, not importance. Essential ions support structure, catalysis, signaling, osmotic balance and transport; deficiency and excess can both be harmful.

Na⁺ and K⁺ establish membrane gradients and support electrical signaling. Mg²⁺ is central to chlorophyll and activates enzymes; Ca²⁺ supports bones, signaling and muscle contraction. Fe occurs in heme proteins for oxygen transport and electron transfer. Cu and Zn are enzyme cofactors; Zn also supports structural protein motifs. Ni, Co and Cr have specialized biological roles depending on organism and chemical form; cobalt is part of vitamin B₁₂.

Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase uses ATP to export three Na⁺ ions and import two K⁺ ions per cycle, maintaining gradients and contributing to membrane potential. Secondary transport can use a gradient rather than directly hydrolyzing ATP. Sodium-glucose cotransport brings glucose into some epithelial cells together with Na⁺; the Na⁺ gradient is maintained by the ATPase. Distinguish the primary active pump from gradient-coupled transport.

Toxicity depends on dose, chemical species, route, duration and biological context. Excess iron can promote oxidative damage; arsenic, mercury compounds, lead and cadmium can disrupt enzymes or tissues and may accumulate. Prevention includes safe water and food, occupational controls and responsible e-waste handling. Metal exposure requires public-health and clinical expertise, not home treatment.
keyPoints: Macro- and micronutrient refer to required amount, not importance.
Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase exports 3 Na⁺ and imports 2 K⁺ per ATP cycle.
Sodium-glucose cotransport uses the Na⁺ gradient; it is not itself the ATP-driven pump.
Biological function and toxicity depend on concentration and chemical form.
Iron, arsenic, mercury, lead and cadmium are toxicity examples in this unit.
practiceQuestions: Distinguish macronutrients from micronutrients and give one example of each.
Describe Na⁺/K⁺ pump stoichiometry and why its Na⁺ gradient supports glucose uptake.
Give two biological roles each for Mg²⁺, Ca²⁺ and Fe ions.
Explain why an essential metal is not safe in unlimited amounts.
summary: Metal ions are essential in regulated amounts for transport, catalysis, structure and signaling. Distinguish ion roles, ATP-driven pumping, gradient-coupled transport and dose-dependent toxicity.
